some solutions for the disk, characterized by extremely high $N_{\mathrm{H2O}}$ and low $T_{\mathrm{dust}}<50$ K, yielded significant likelihood.
we use the prior $P(\mathbf{a})=0$ whenever a model component with $T_{\mathrm{dust}}<60$ K and $X_{\mathrm{H2O}}>3\times10^{-5}$ is found

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: The core may be powered by a buried AGN or by a compact starburst.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Insufficient nuclear dynamical mass may reflect lower inclination or nonrotational support.

evidence.quote: This discrepancy can be attributed to a lower inclination of the nuclear disk relative to that of the host galaxy
Alternatively, $V_{\mathrm{rot}}$ could underestimate $M_{\mathrm{dyn}}$ if the nuclear gas is not rotationally supported, but supported by radiation pressure and turbulence.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Low-intensity broad CO may be an outflow counterpart, but a bar-overshooting shock is considered more plausible.

evidence.quote: It is thus possible that this CO component represents the low-velocity counterpart of the CO outflow

a more plausible interpretation suggested by the limiting velocities and also by the location of this component ahead of the bar major axis, is that it represents the kinematic effect of the strong shock

how_they_decided_enough.value: Three components yield reduced chi-squared 1.0–1.4, versus a minimum 2.3 for two; more complex nuclear velocity fields were limited by resolution and beam smearing.

evidence.quote: The values of $\chi_{\mathrm{red}}^2$ for the best-fit $10^3$ combinations are in the range $1.0-1.4$, indicating that three components provide a good fit and more are not needed.
the minimum value of $\chi_{\mathrm{red}}^2$ significantly increases to 2.3 when only 2 components are used.
We have not attempted more complex velocity fields given our limited spatial resolution and significant beam smearing.

referee_caveats_inferred: The abundance prior can materially affect disk solutions; reproduce both the initial and adopted priors.
CO inflow depends on the adopted conversion factor, planar geometry, fitted velocity curves, and ±50 km s^-1 selection.
The reservoir/travel-time inflow check shares inputs with the instantaneous estimate and is not wholly independent.
No quantitative uncertainty budget is supplied for the tabulated CO inflow rates.
The unresolved core and nuclear dynamical-mass discrepancy weaken unique geometric and power-source interpretations.
Proto-pseudobulge formation is an interpretation of present structure and gas motions rather than a directly observed evolutionary outcome.
